caption:
A $1.5 billion investment in the skies. US-Bangla is adding 21 new Boeing aircraft to its fleet.

US-Bangla Airlines has announced the acquisition of 21 new Boeing aircraft in a deal worth approximately $1.5 billion, marking one of the largest fleet expansions in Bangladesh's aviation history.

The new fleet will consist of 15 Boeing 737-8 aircraft and six Boeing 737-800 aircraft, all of which are scheduled to be delivered in phases by the end of 2027 under a leasing programme.

The expansion will enable the airline to launch flights to new destinations, including cities in India, Sri Lanka, Nepal, China, China, South Korea, Japan, Kuwait, Bahrain, Oman, and Saudi Arabia.

Mohammad Abdullah Al Mamun, managing director of US-Bangla Group, stated that the investment reflects a vision to transform the airline into a fully integrated global aviation group.

US Ambassador Brent T Christensen noted that the airline plans to send approximately 200 Bangladeshi pilots to the US for advanced training as part of the investment in people.

Humaiun Kobir, the prime minister’s foreign affairs adviser, and Rashiduzzaman Millat, state minister for civil aviation and tourism, expressed government support for the aviation sector's growth.
